origin.description: Detect whether a regular expression matches each string.
origin.usage: stri_detect_regex(str, pattern, negate = FALSE, max_count = -1, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, report strings that do not match.

arguments.name: max_count
arguments.text: Stop after this many results of interest. Later elements are NA. Negative means no limit.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. negate flips a real match and does not flip a missing result. max_count counts only results that are TRUE after negate, and it visits elements in stringi's pattern order. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
origin.value: A logical vector. A missing result is NA.
origin.example:
result <- stri_detect_regex(c("stringi R", "R STRINGI", "123"), "R.")
cat(paste0('stri_detect_regex(c("stringi R", "R STRINGI", "123"), "R.") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Detect whether a regular expression matches each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, report strings that do not match.

arguments.name: max_count
arguments.text: Stop after this many results of interest. Later elements are NA. Negative means no limit.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

translation.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. negate flips a real match and does not flip a missing result. max_count counts only results that are TRUE after negate, and it visits elements in stringi's pattern order. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_detect_regex
result = stri_detect_regex(["stringi R", "R STRINGI", "123"], "R.")
words = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print('stri_detect_regex(c("stringi R", "R STRINGI", "123"), "R.") returns ' + words + '.')
